look_here_first: LOOK FOR THE NEEDLE-LIKE LEAVES AND HAIRY FRUIT FIRST. Beetle spurge (Euphorbia eriantha) is an UPRIGHT or ascending desert spurge, not a creeping sandmat. Most main-stem leaves are ALTERNATE, linear or narrowly elliptic (20–55 × 1–3 mm) with only 2–4 tiny teeth near the tip. At the flowering ends, 2–3 linear green BRACTS are opposite or whorled; don't mistakenly call all stem foliage opposite. The fruit is surprisingly conspicuous: an oblong, commonly white-HAIRY 3-lobed capsule 4.4–4.9 mm long, often green/white mottled (photographed clearly). Tiny cyathia are clustered among fruits, with gland appendages described by Flora of North America as WHITISH, densely hairy, divided into 5–12 narrow fringes and curled INWARD over the glands; our existing photos show the hairy flowering clusters, but not individual inward-turning hairs/fringes with certainty. Compare E. exstipulata: usually conspicuous leaf teeth and white/pink appendages that do NOT fold over the gland. Genuine mature seeds are 2.8–4.1 mm, pitted/warty and carry a caruncle; do NOT point to a striped green CAPSULE and call it a seed. FNA western-desert ecology is not evidence of Hays County nativity; native-range review remains paused.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Euphorbiaceae, Euphorbia sect. Poinsettia (subsect. Erianthae). Cyathia are tiny cup-like reproductive units, not ordinary true-petaled flowers; fruit is a capsular spurge.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Annual or short-lived perennial with taproot; erect to ascending 10–75 cm; curving branches. Rocky desert washes and slopes, not a presumed common Hays County species.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Main stem leaves ALTERNATE (basal node may appear opposite), 20–55 × 1–3 mm linear to narrow linear-elliptic with pronounced midvein; 2–4 tiny teeth close to the apex or practically entire to naked eye. Lower face sometimes short soft hairs; upper face often nearly glabrous.

key_traits.label: Bracts
key_traits.text: Upper flowering bracts 2–3, OPPOSITE or WHORLED, linear green and leaf-like, subtending terminal few-cyathium branches; distinguish these from the actual alternate main stem leaves.

key_traits.label: Cyathia
key_traits.text: Terminal cymose group, tiny hairs cover the involucre; 2–5 commonly 4–5 green-maroon shallowly cupped glands, 0.5–0.6 mm wide, commonly hidden by WHITE/gray dense hairy appendages folded inward over glands.

key_traits.label: Gland appendages
key_traits.text: Extraordinary whitish hood-like appendages 0.5–1 mm, cut into 5–12 long fine subulate fingers, densely whitish-hairy, CURLING OVER glands, vs E. exstipulata appendages that do not cover glands.

key_traits.label: Ovary capsules
key_traits.text: Oblong-ovoid approx 4.4–4.9 × 3.5–4.1 mm 3-lobed fruit, canescent (covered in short white/gray hairs) with sometimes hairless patches; much larger and hairier than a tiny sandmat's fruit.

key_traits.label: Seeds
key_traits.text: Mature true seeds oblong or ovoid, 2.8–4.1 × 2–2.4 mm, mottled black and gray or light brown, flattened dorsiventrally, coarsely tuberculate/pitted, with an obvious pale caruncle at attachment end. Do not confuse developing capsule patterns with detached seed surfaces.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: ALTERNATE, linear near-needlelike 2–5.5 cm × 1–3 mm leaves

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Upper opposite/whorled GREEN leaf-like flowering bracts (not showy white bracts)

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Tiny almost concealed terminal cyathia with HAIRY white appendages folded inward over glands

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Large white-gray hairy, often mottled oblong 3-lobed capsules

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Mature large 2.8–4.1mm visibly warted/mottled seeds with caruncle

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Generally erect or ascending instead of creeping sandmat
